result.topic_en: Latin draft (page 26) of the commentary on Riemann's Paris prize essay: it derives the curvature measure from Gauss's form of the line element, checks it against the earlier expression, remarks that the calculations confirming the propositions are incomplete, and begins asking when temperature can depend on only one variable besides time.

obtinemus, quam dedit Gauss elemento lineari h[?]
in superficie quacunque:
$ds^2 = dr^2 + m^2 d\psi^2$
(Disquisitiones generales circa superficies curvas
art. 19), unde habetur mensura curvaturae:
$k = -\frac{1}{m}\frac{\partial^2 m}{\partial r^2}$
At in puncto $r=0$ habetur, si quidem superficies
in hoc puncto habet curvaturam continuam:
$m = 0 \quad \frac{\partial m}{\partial r} = 1 \quad \frac{\partial^2 m}{\partial r^2} = 0$
unde fit in puncto 0:
$k = -\frac{\partial^3 m}{\partial r^3}$
[-Pro functione $\mu$-] Hinc sequitur pro functione
$\mu$ in eodem puncto:
$\mu = 1 \quad \frac{\partial \mu}{\partial r} = 0 \qquad k = -\frac{3}{2}\frac{\partial^2 \mu}{\partial r^2}$
Primis duabus harum aequationum satisfieri ex
aequationibus (3), (5) facile sequitur. Tertia nobis
[-praebet-] {+concluditur+}:
$k = -\frac{3}{2}\, \frac{\sum_{\iota\iota'\iota''\iota'''}\left(\frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota\iota'}}{\partial x_{\iota''}\partial x_{\iota'''}}\right)_0 c_{\iota''} c_{\iota'''}\, dx_\iota dx_{\iota'}}{\sum_{\iota\iota'} a^0_{\iota\iota'}\, dx_\iota dx_{\iota'}}$
vel etiam:
$k = -\frac{3}{2}\, \frac{\sum\left(\frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota\iota'}}{\partial x_{\iota''}\partial x_{\iota'''}}\right)_0 c_{\iota''} c_{\iota'''}\, dx_\iota dx_{\iota'}}{\sum_{\iota\iota'} a^0_{\iota\iota'} c_\iota c_{\iota'} \sum_{\iota\iota'} a^0_{\iota\iota'}\, dx_\iota dx_{\iota'} - \left(\sum_{\iota\iota'} a^0_{\iota\iota'}\, c_\iota dx_{\iota'}\right)^2}$
Quam expressionem cum ea quam supra invenimus,
identicam esse facile perspicitur.
[margin, faint: quae exp. ... identica esse apparet.]

nondum contigit. Gratissimum nobis fores[?], si alius
forsan [-meliori-] {+feliciori cum+} successu rem iterum aggrederetur.
[margin, faint: Si alius forsan [-melior-] cum successu rem [-...-] denuo aggredietur, optime de analysi meceretur[?]. ... aggredi suscipit[?]]
Quod ut facilius eveniat, hic afferemus, [-quae-] {+quantum+}
ex iis, quae auctor [-reliquit-] scripta reliquit,
explanare potuimus.
Primum quaeramus, quibusnam in casibus temperatura
u praeter tempus ab una tantum variabili pendere

necessarios, prolixissimos ut videtur, plane enodare

items.english: We have not yet succeeded in fully working out the calculations needed to confirm these propositions, which seem very lengthy.
To make this easier, we will present here as much as we have been able to explain from what the author left in writing.
